summary: Iteration 55 — Batch-Based Weekly Sending Planner is fully green end-to-end. BACKEND: 21/21 pytest pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration_55_batch_planner.py. Spec 4000-leads example produces exact expected output (5 batches × 800 leads, daily_capacity=800, total_emails=12000, status=Ready, 15 schedule rows all Ready). Step-1 dates land on Mon Sep 14 → Fri Sep 18. Follow-up alignment: Batch1 step2=2026-09-21 (Mon), step3=2026-09-28 (Mon); Batch5 step3=2026-10-02 (Fri). Uneven divide 4250→[800,800,800,800,800,250]. Weekday snapping: with Mon-Fri sending_days delay_days=5 from Mon Sep 14 snaps Sat Sep 19 forward to Mon Sep 21; with weekends allowed it stays on Sat Sep 19. Real inbox pool mode: pool_source='real_inbox_pool', daily_capacity matches sum of inbox daily_limits; all-unknown account_ids → 400. Validation: leads=0→422; sending_days=[]→200 (Pydantic-permissive, planner falls back to Mon-Fri default); start_date='not-a-date'→400; missing both pool options→400 with detail mentioning 'account_ids', 'accounts', and 'daily_limit_per_account'. Capacity conflict (1600/2/delay=1): row on 2026-09-15 shows required_capacity=1600 vs available=800, status downgrades to 'Partial Capacity', warning contains all 4 strings (Capacity exceeded, Required, Available, Shortfall) + the date. Exports: xlsx returns spreadsheetml content-type with 2 sheets (Summary first, Schedule second), Schedule has exactly 16 rows (header+15) with headers matching spec; csv returns text/csv with 16 lines; format=pdf → 400. Permissions: non-permitted drip.tester→403 on both /planner/batch and /planner/batch/export. Regression: standard /planner still Ready for 1000/3/60, /summary + /inboxes intact. FRONTEND (Playwright via Mongo session injection): /infrastructure Capacity Planner section now has a mode toggle (planner-mode-standard | planner-mode-batch). Switching to batch reveals batch-planner-form with all 11 input testids (batch-leads, batch-steps, batch-delay, batch-accounts, batch-per-account, batch-start-date, batch-tz, batch-sending-days-row, batch-daily-capacity-readout, batch-include-weekends, batch-run-btn) AND all 7 weekday buttons (batch-day-mon through batch-day-sun). batch-daily-capacity-readout shows live '800' for 20×40. Running the spec 4000-leads payload renders batch-plan-result panel with: batch-status-ready badge, '2026-09-14 → 2026-10-02 · 19 days' header, 4 summary cards (Total leads 4000 / Total batches 5 / Daily capacity 800 / Total emails 12000), batch-list with 5 batch-card-{1..5} cards labelled Mon..Fri Sep 14..18, batch-schedule-table with 15 batch-row-* rows all showing Ready. batch-export-xlsx-btn and batch-export-csv-btn both fire 200 downloads with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="RouteMail_Batch_Plan_<date>.xlsx|csv" and correct Content-Types (spreadsheetml / text/csv). Conflict payload 1600/2/delay=1 surfaces batch-warnings panel with 'Capacity exceeded on 2026-09-15. Required: 1,600 · Available: 800 · Shortfall: 800' AND batch-status-partial-capacity pill. Standard-mode toggle re-mounts existing planner-leads input and unmounts batch-planner-form. Phase-1/2/3 regression testids (nav-infrastructure, infra-allocator-section, infra-planner-section, allocator-required-input, allocator-run-btn, planner-run-btn) all still present.

critical_code_review_comments: infra_phase3.py — _batch_plan is a single clean function (~200 lines) with clear stage comments (1.pool → 2.carve → 3.step1 → 4.project → 5.rollups). Pure function, no side effects, easy to reason about.
_next_sending_day helper correctly caps at 14 iterations as a safety net — guards against bad sending_days input without raising.

Capacity conflict logic uses self_load aggregator (defaultdict) to combine batches landing on the same day — verified at runtime for the 1600/2/d=1 spec case (Tue 09-15: 1600 required vs 800 available → Partial Capacity).

Status downgrade is correctly hierarchical: any 'Insufficient Capacity' row → overall Insufficient; else any 'Partial Capacity' → overall Partial; else Ready. Per-row rule: available>=required→Ready; available>=row.leads but <required→Partial; else Insufficient.
Export endpoint streams BytesIO without holding the whole workbook in memory longer than necessary; both xlsx and csv go through StreamingResponse with correct Content-Disposition.

Pydantic validation: leads ge=1, steps ge=1 le=20, delay_days ge=1 le=90, account_ids/accounts/daily_limit_per_account all Optional — XOR validation enforced at handler layer with helpful 400 detail mentioning both options. Test verified.

Frontend BatchPlannerForm: 1 component file (~280 lines added inline at bottom of Infrastructure.jsx). All 7 weekday buttons + include-weekends convenience toggle wired to a single sending_days Set state — clean.
Pre-existing lint warnings (set-state-in-effect lines 88+149) noted in brief are unchanged — not introduced by iter-55.
